summary: Part 2 of the 11.1 Dashboard (Seller) video (05:01 to 09:10). The trainer finishes the Claims coverage KPI on the Performance tab, then walks through the Scoring tab (the Next score calculation table built from four KPIs), then the Analysis tab (the orders, defects, days-to-solve and open claims behind each KPI), and ends by telling sellers to contact their account manager. All screens are a demo seller (URL contains demo=Seller+ABC and supplier=7), so every number is a sample snapshot. The charts run from Jun 15 to Aug 31* (June to August data), so the figures must not be read as a current score. All 27 frames listed in the pack were opened and checked against the narration.

facts.statement: Claims coverage is, of the claims you were given to solve, the share you have actually solved, judged as of today.

evidence.quote: Methodology: Of the claims you were given to solve, the share you have actually solved, judged as of today.

facts.statement: Claims coverage is counted against the month (monthly view) or the week (weekly view) in which the claim was received.

evidence.quote: Methodology: Counted against the month the claim was received.
Methodology (weekly): Counted against the week the claim was received.

facts.statement: The claims coverage divisor is received minus cancelled: a withdrawn (cancelled) claim never had to be solved, so it counts neither for nor against the seller.

evidence.quote: Methodology: The divisor is received minus cancelled: a claim that was withdrawn never had to be solved, so it counts neither for nor against you.

facts.statement: A claim counts as solved when a warranty claim's device ships back, or a return claim's money reaches the customer. These are the same endings Days to solve uses.

evidence.quote: Methodology: A warranty is solved when the device ships back, a return when the money reaches the customer - the same endings Days to solve uses, so the two reconcile claim for claim.

facts.statement: A recent month (or week) always reads low on claims coverage: a claim received last month (or week) has had fewer days to be solved than one received months ago.

evidence.quote: Methodology: A recent month always reads low: a claim received last month has had days to be solved, one from months ago has had months.
Methodology (weekly): A recent week always reads low: a claim received last week has had days to solve, one from months ago has had months.

facts.statement: Claims coverage is keyed on the repair partner, meaning the claims you repaired. Change-of-mind claims and claims ruled invalid are excluded.

evidence.quote: Methodology: Keyed on the repair partner: the claims you repaired. Change-of-mind claims and claims ruled invalid are excluded.

terms.meaning: Total of the four KPI contributions for the next score calculation (-2.5% in the snapshot). Shown at the bottom of the Scoring tab's table.
The change to the score that a KPI value produces, shown in the Score impact column of the Next score calculation table (for example -10% for On time at 67%).
Share of the score a KPI carries: On time 10%, Defect rate 60%, Days to solve 20%, Claims coverage 10%.
Score impact multiplied by weight; the contributions add up to the Next score.
The time window a KPI is measured over (for example Week -2 = 17-23 Aug in the snapshot). Shown in the Period column.
Expandable definition panel under each chart or table, giving the rule used for the number.
Missed = orders counted late in the window. Implied: judged = orders the on-time KPI considered. Snapshot: 55 missed of 166 judged, 67% on time.
Per-row threshold the row was judged against: <= 5 for SA rows, < 3 for the ZA and AE shipment rows shown in the snapshot.
Working days, weekends excluded. Used for days to ship and days to deliver on the on-time analysis.
A miss tag for an order that shipped but was never marked delivered and is now past its deadline.
Claims counted against orders in the window: one row per order, so two claims on one order count as one defect. Snapshot: 69 of 1,221 orders = 5.7%.
Claim type where the money goes back to the customer; days to solve ends when the refund reaches the customer.
Claim type where the device ships back; days to solve ends when the device ships back.
Share of claims given to solve that are actually solved, judged as of today. Snapshot: 120 of 137 = 88%.
The claims count used as the denominator for claims coverage: received claims minus cancelled claims.
Chart categories on claims coverage: Solved = solved claims; Still open = unsolved claims; To solve = Solved plus Still open.
Calendar days from the claim date to the ending that counts (refund for returns, shipped back for warranties; refund day if a warranty ended in a refund).
For an unsolved claim, the number of days it has been open, listed in the Claims coverage analysis.

Current stage of a claim. Stages seen on screen include: 2. In transit; 3. Under QC; 4. Invalid claim; 7. Refunded; 8. Under process; 9. To ship back; 10. Shipped back; 16. Under collection; 18. Under revision; 19. Expert revision; 20. Invalid claim confirmed.
Country code of the order: SA, ZA, AE (shown in the MARKET column and the country filter).
Country filter presets shown above the country flags.
Implied: category filter preset that limits the chart to the top three categories.
The basis for claims coverage: the claims you repaired. Change-of-mind claims and claims ruled invalid are excluded.

asr_fixes.basis: On the screen the On time row shows Contribution -1% (t00326.jpg, t00354.jpg); the trainer reads it as a negative figure too ('minus 1% score' at 06:34).

unclear.issue: The On time KPI is 67%. The narration says it is higher than 65 so it takes that row, but the screen shows score impact -10%. In the Scoring table the -50% row holds 65% and the -10% row holds 80%, so 67% falls between them. The rule for matching a KPI to a row is not stated, so no matching rule is given as a fact.

The trainer says the UAE shipment took 5 days, but on the screen the 102740-3 row shows Days to ship (WD) = 3 with SLA < 3. Order 22 Aug to shipped 27 Aug is 5 calendar days, while the column is in working days. The unit the trainer uses is not clear, so the figure is not stated as a fact.

In the Scoring table, the Days to solve column reads 8 at +3% and 6 at +4%, then 8 again at +5%. The +5% value is higher than the +4% value while the rest of the column falls as the score rises. This may be a misread or a table error; not stated as a fact.
The monthly claims coverage tooltip (Jan 26) shows All claims 16.5, Returns 16.8 and Warranties 16.3. The unit and meaning of these numbers are not explained on screen or in the narration.
Axis labels such as 'Aug 31*' and 'Sep*' carry an asterisk that is not explained anywhere on screen or in the narration.
Parts of the on-time explanatory note are small in the frames, so the wording of the SA and outside-SA rules is read from frame t00381.jpg and stated at medium confidence.

The on-time chart legend reads AE (<=2) and ZA (<=2), but the shipment rows for ZA-74346-1 and 102740-3 show SLA '< 3' on the Analysis tab (t00431.jpg). The legend and the table use different thresholds for the same markets; this is not resolved here, so no single AE or ZA threshold is stated as fact.
GMV values show a currency symbol on screen (a glyph shown in front of the GMV figures); the narration never names the currency. The currency is not stated.
The claims table stage 'Sent to Naif' is not explained; it is unclear whether it is a partner name or a stage.
The header chip 'Pepe' is shown next to Buybox open and WhatsApp and is not explained. It is not treated as the account manager's name.
Narration 'On the analysis tab, we will detail {everyone,?} each of these four KPIs' has an unclear word; no fact depends on it.
The KPI header 'Aug 26' is shown as the monthly period label. It is not explicitly stated whether it means August 2026 or another reading.

outdated.signal: All figures are a demo seller snapshot (URL demo=Seller+ABC) from June to August data, with fixed periods such as 17-23 Aug, 13 Jul - 23 Aug, 22 Jun - 23 Aug and 17-30 Aug. They are examples and must not be read as a current score.

Claim IDs and order numbers on the defect, days-to-solve and claims coverage tables (for example IpQn95, PUPD081, SA-119945-1, ZSBZ876). No customer name, phone, email or address is visible in any frame.
The header chip 'Pepe' and the 'Sent to Naif' stage may be personal names. Not confirmed; check before sharing.

Presenter webcam overlay in the lower-left corner of every frame, and browser tabs and bookmarks visible at the top (Revibe CX - Login, Select a Date & Time - Calendar, Share on WhatsApp; bookmarks such as Interactive Brokers and Carta). Crop or blur these before the material is shown to sellers.
